chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Feeding the prisoner is a right upon the one who imprisoned him, and even if he intended killing him the next day. So it is befitting that he feeds him, and quenches him, and shades him, and is kind with him, whether he was an Infidel or someone else.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a prisoner in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Reported by Zurarah, a prominent companion of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith underscores the universality of the captor's duty to provide sustenance and comfort, irrespective of the prisoner's faith or imminent fate. It highlights the Shia emphasis on *ihsan* (excellence in conduct) and justice, ensuring that the prisoner's rights are fulfilled even during the interim period before execution or ransom.
